record.original_question: Classify all two-orbit polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space H^3.

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Classify all two-orbit polyhedra in H^3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}^3$ denote hyperbolic 3-space. A polyhedron $P \subset \mathbb{H}^3$ is a 3-dimensional polytope (a properly stratified polytopal complex with vertices, edges, and 2-faces) embedded in $\mathbb{H}^3$. A flag of $P$ is a triple $(v, e, f)$ consisting of a vertex $v$, an edge $e$, and a 2-face $f$ with $v \subset e \subset f$. The symmetry group $G(P)$ of $P$ is the group of isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$ that map $P$ to itself; it acts on the set of flags of $P$. The polyhedron $P$ is said to be a two-orbit polyhedron if $G(P)$ acts on the set of flags of $P$ with exactly two orbits.

Classify, up to isometry of $\mathbb{H}^3$, all two-orbit polyhedra in $\mathbb{H}^3$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published classification of two-orbit polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space was located. While there are well-known characterizations of compact, ideal, and hyperideal convex polyhedra in $\mathbb{H}^3$ (Andreev, Rivin, Hodgson, etc.), these do not address the flag-orbit (two-orbit) symmetry classification. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hyperideal polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space
status_evidence.snippet: Hyperideal polyhedra are non-compact polyhedra in H^3 with vertices outside H^3.
status_evidence.claim: Existing characterization work focuses on convex/ideal/hyperideal polyhedra, not on flag-orbit symmetry classification.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of compact convex polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of compact convex hyperbolic polyhedra by dihedral angles.
status_evidence.claim: Known classifications concern dihedral angle / metric characterizations rather than two-orbit symmetry types.
